title: A letter to a friend

prepTasks.word: I am writing to tell you...

writingModel:
Dear Aisha,

How are you? I hope you and your family are well. I am writing to tell you all about my new apartment here in Uralsk! I moved in three weeks ago with my friend Zara from my Economics group. I have been so busy with university that this is my first chance to write a proper letter. I miss you so much and I think about our school days in Kokshetau all the time!

First, let me describe our apartment. There are three rooms: a living room, a bedroom, and a kitchen. There is also one bathroom and a small hallway. The apartment is on the third floor of a quiet building, just a ten-minute walk from WKU. There isn't a lift, so we walk up three flights of stairs every day — great exercise! The rent is 80,000 tenge per month, so we each pay 40,000. It is much more expensive than the dormitory, but we have so much more freedom and space!

My favourite room is the living room. There is a comfortable blue sofa where Zara and I watch films on Friday evenings. There are two bookshelves full of our textbooks and novels. There is a big window that lets in beautiful morning light — I love studying there with a cup of tea! There is also a small balcony with four potted plants. Zara brought them from her home in Almaty and she waters them every single morning. Do you have any plants at home?

The kitchen is small but we cook together every evening. There is a round table with four chairs, so we sometimes invite classmates for dinner. There is a washing machine too, which is very convenient — no more trips to the laundry! There isn't a dishwasher, but I do not really mind. Last week, Zara made beshbarmak and we invited three friends from our group. There were five people around our small kitchen table and it was so much fun! You would love Zara — she is kind, funny, and an amazing cook.

I really love living here, Aisha. It feels like our own little home. There is a small park just around the corner where I sometimes walk in the evenings to clear my head after studying. There are some beautiful old trees there and it reminds me of the park near our school in Kokshetau. I miss our walks there so much!

Please write back and tell me everything about your life. How is university? Are there any interesting people in your group? I cannot wait to hear from you.

With love and many hugs,
Kamila
